summary: Adds a `stash auth login` command (device-code flow + device bind via the new native dependency @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2) and makes authentication a mandatory first step of `stash init`. The init next-steps and README no longer tell users to set CS_* credentials and claim the SDK and CLI use the saved token in ~/.cipherstash/auth.json for local development, but `stash secrets`, the Secrets class and LockContext at head still read only CS_* env vars / cipherstash.toml (the TOML docs were also removed). The change also pins runtime dependencies to exact versions that downgrade @byteslice/result (0.2.2 -> 0.2.0) and evlog (1.11.0 -> 1.9.0) for the published library. Nothing touches the encryption path, payload format or key handling directly. No tests cover the CLI, and no CI results were provided. Impact is medium: onboarding and CLI failures that users notice, not data or security failures. A reviewer should check the documented credential contract, how eagerly the native module loads, the non-interactive init path, and the dependency downgrades.

behaviour_changes.description: New CLI command `stash auth login`: prompts for a region from a hard-coded list, runs the device code flow (prints the code and URL, opens a browser, polls for a token that @cipherstash/auth persists to ~/.cipherstash/auth.json), then binds the device to the default Keyset. A bind failure exits with code 1.

`stash init` now always runs authenticateStep first (region select, device-code login, device bind). It cannot be skipped and does not detect an existing token or CS_* credentials. Every init therefore needs an interactive terminal, a browser and network access before any scaffolding happens.

The init next-steps (base and supabase providers) no longer tell users to create an account and set CS_WORKSPACE_CRN/CS_CLIENT_ID/CS_CLIENT_KEY/CS_CLIENT_ACCESS_KEY. The README now says local development needs no env vars or credentials files, says the SDK and CLI use ~/.cipherstash/auth.json, and removes the TOML config section and the note that the CLI reads CS_* env vars.

Adds runtime dependency @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2, a native package with per-platform optional binaries (darwin arm64/x64, linux arm64-gnu, x64-gnu, x64-musl, win32 x64). It is imported statically by the CLI entry point, so it loads for every `stash` command. It is also installed for every consumer of @cipherstash/stack, because it is a regular dependency.

Runtime dependencies of the published library change from caret ranges to exact pins. The lockfile resolution goes down from @byteslice/result 0.2.2 to 0.2.0 (used by every encryption operation's withResult) and from evlog 1.11.0 to 1.9.0 (used by the library logger).

failure_scenarios.title: Docs and init promise credential-free local dev, but secrets CLI/API and LockContext still require CS_* env vars
failure_scenarios.trigger: A new user follows the updated README or the init next-steps: runs `stash init` or `stash auth login`, sets no CS_* vars and no cipherstash.toml, then runs `stash secrets ...`, constructs `Secrets`, or uses LockContext.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The next-steps lists drop the CS_* setup instruction (base.ts:14, supabase.ts:18), and the README says the SDK and CLI use ~/.cipherstash/auth.json (README.md:451, 497). `stash secrets` getConfig still exits when CS_WORKSPACE_CRN/CS_CLIENT_ID/CS_CLIENT_KEY are missing (helpers.ts:33-61). Secrets throws without CS_* values (secrets/index.ts:179-188). loadWorkSpaceId, used by LockContext, throws without CS_WORKSPACE_CRN or cipherstash.toml (config/index.ts:59-92, identity/index.ts:62). The README section that documented cipherstash.toml was deleted even though the code still reads it. The shipped stash-encryption skill still documents CS_* vars.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Users get 'Missing required environment variables' or 'You have not defined a workspace CRN' errors right after an onboarding flow that told them no credentials are needed, and the docs no longer say where to put them. Agent skills copied into customer repos give guidance that conflicts with the README. The failures are loud; no data or security effect.
missing_verification: An end-to-end check that `stash auth login` followed by `stash secrets list` (and Encryption()/LockContext) works with no CS_* vars set.
Confirmation of whether protect-ffi 0.21.0 newClient reads ~/.cipherstash/auth.json.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Make the docs match the code: state which surfaces support the auth.json token (only the encryption client, if protect-ffi supports it) and keep CS_*/cipherstash.toml instructions for secrets and LockContext. Alternatively, add auth.json support to those paths before claiming it. Update skills/stash-encryption/SKILL.md in the same release.

failure_scenarios.title: Native @cipherstash/auth loaded eagerly breaks every stash command on platforms without a prebuilt binary
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs any `stash` command (including `stash secrets` or `stash --help`) on a platform with no @cipherstash/auth binary in 0.34.2, e.g. linux-arm64-musl (Alpine on ARM) or win32-arm64, or where optional dependencies were skipped at install.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: stash.ts:7 statically imports commands/auth/index.js, which imports login.ts. login.ts:2-3 does `import auth from '@cipherstash/auth'` at module top level, so the package is resolved before main() runs. The lockfile lists only six platform binaries (pnpm-lock.yaml:467-497). The CLI bundle keeps dependencies external (tsup.config.ts:26-41). If the package's loader throws when no binary matches, which is typical of napi packages but not verified here, the error happens at import time, before the main().catch handler can catch it.
failure_scenarios.consequence: `stash secrets` and `stash init` stop working on those platforms, even for users who never use auth. Before this change, those commands did not need this module. The failure is loud; a fix needs a new release.
missing_verification: A smoke test of `stash --help` / `stash secrets` on a platform without a matching binary, or inspection of @cipherstash/auth's loader behaviour.
A CLI smoke test in CI on each supported OS.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Lazy-load @cipherstash/auth (dynamic import inside login/bindDevice) so only `auth` and `init` depend on it, and show a clear message when the platform is unsupported.

failure_scenarios.title: Mandatory interactive device-code auth makes `stash init` unusable non-interactively or offline
failure_scenarios.trigger: `stash init` runs in CI, in a container without a browser, from a coding agent, or by a user who already has CS_* machine credentials or no network access to the auth service.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: authenticateStep is now first in STEPS (init/index.ts:16-22) and always calls selectRegion, login and bindDevice (authenticate.ts:7-12). There is no flag to skip it and no check for an existing token or env credentials. login() waits on pollForToken with no timeout handling of its own (login.ts:32-51). bindDevice() calls process.exit(1) on any error (login.ts:53-65). Any failure therefore aborts init before the connection, schema and forge steps run.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Workflows that used to scaffold a project with `stash init` now hang at a prompt or exit before generating anything. Users with working machine credentials are forced through a browser login and a device bind to the default Keyset that they may not want.
missing_verification: Tests for init with auth skipped, failing or already done.
A check of pollForToken behaviour on expiry or denial (it lives inside @cipherstash/auth and could not be read).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add a `--skip-auth` flag, or skip the step when a valid token or CS_* credentials already exist. Treat a bind failure as a warning in init, or throw an error that the init loop handles, instead of calling process.exit.

failure_scenarios.title: Exact-pin downgrades of @byteslice/result and evlog change library runtime for all consumers
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer installs the new @cipherstash/stack minor version. Their encryption operations now run against @byteslice/result 0.2.0 and evlog 1.9.0 instead of the 0.2.2 and 1.11.0 that the base lockfile resolved.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: package.json:209-213 pins exact versions, and the lockfile moves @byteslice/result to 0.2.0 and evlog to 1.9.0 (pnpm-lock.yaml:406, 1489). withResult wraps every encryption operation's result (e.g. encryption/index.ts:22), and the logger uses initLogger/createRequestLogger plus sampling rates from evlog (utils/logger/index.ts:1-33). Whether 0.2.0 → 0.2.2 or 1.9.0 → 1.11.0 contains behaviour this code relies on is unknown. Exact pins also stop consumers' package managers from deduplicating these packages.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If behaviour differs, the result/failure objects that callers branch on, or the log-level filtering, could change silently for library users. This part of the PR is unrelated to the CLI feature. No evidence of an actual difference was found.
